claims.sourceText: FBI FOIPA cover letter, Request No. 1380241-001, 12 April 2024
claims.text: The FBI's FOIPA cover letter is dated 12 April 2024 and states '449 pages were reviewed and 313 pages are being released'; the release consists of cross-references only, with no main file on Corso.

The FBI file records Corso's appearance before the Senate Internal Security Subcommittee on 15 May 1961, testimony which 'consisted primarily of his reading into the Committee's records the entries from personal and private office diaries that he kept during his service with the Operations Coordinating Board from 1953 to 1957.'

In 1955 Gen. Arthur S. Trudeau told the FBI that 'Colonel Philip Corso, then assigned to the Operations Coordinating Board, would be in a position to elaborate ... as he, Corso, had actually accumulated the information' on a list of alleged Fabian Socialists. The FBI reviewed its files on those named and found 'insufficient evidence to prove the validity of the allegation.' This corroborates the OCB posting from a record that is not Corso's own.

The FBI file records that in February 1964, a rumour that Lee Harvey Oswald had been a paid FBI informant was traced to Corso, who 'admitted that he had passed out information concerning Oswald's alleged connection with the FBI', refused to name his sources, and 'emphasized the fact that his allegations had been strictly deductions and had no basis in fact.'
The FBI files state plainly: 'Our files do not reveal that Corso has been investigated by this Bureau.'
